API Reference

Flask app and routes — app

Routes registered by app.create_app():

Route

Method

Response

/ and /analysis

GET

200 HTML Analysis page

/pull-data

POST

200 {"ok": true, "count": N}; 409 {"busy": true}; 500 on failure

/update-analysis

POST

200 {"ok": true}; 409 {"busy": true} while a pull runs

Route handlers

app.analysis()[source]

GET / and GET /analysis: render the Analysis page.

Shows the latest snapshot stored by Update Analysis (or computed on first load), the Pull Data / Update Analysis buttons, and the current pull status.

Return type:

str

app.pull_data()[source]

POST /pull-data: scrape new records and pass them to the loader.

Returns:

200 {"ok": true, "count": N} on success; 409 {"ok": false, "busy": true} if a pull is already running; 500 {"ok": false, "busy": false, "error": ...} if scraping or loading fails (the loader’s single transaction leaves no partial writes).

Return type:

Any

app.update_analysis()[source]

POST /update-analysis: re-run the analysis query and store the new snapshot.

Returns:

200 {"ok": true} when not busy; 409 {"ok": false, "busy": true} while a pull is running, in which case the stored snapshot is left unchanged.

Return type:

Any

App factory and helpers

app.create_app(config=None, *, scraper=None, loader=None, query=None)[source]

Build the Flask app and register its routes.

Parameters:

  • config (dict[str, Any] | None) – Flask config overrides. DATABASE_URL repoints all database access.

  • scraper (Callable[[], list[dict[str, Any]]] | None) – Returns raw applicant records; defaults to scrape_new_records().

  • loader (Callable[[list[dict[str, Any]]], int] | None) – Writes records to PostgreSQL and returns the count; defaults to load_data.load_into_database().

  • query (Callable[[], dict[str, Any]] | None) – Returns the analysis snapshot; defaults to orm_queries.analysis_snapshot().

Return type:

Flask

scrape.scrape_data(html_file)[source]

Collect records from saved browser-captured HTML as the real working approach.

The assignment note indicates that direct urllib or Selenium scraping is often blocked by Cloudflare, while a hybrid browser capture approach works reliably for a given page. This function therefore expects a saved HTML file that was captured from a user-verified browser session.

Parameters:

html_file (str | Path)

Return type:

List[Dict[str, Any]]

Browser capture — auto_next_pages and capture_chrome_html

Capture Grad Cafe survey pages from a user-verified Chrome tab via the DevTools protocol.

The loop saves each page’s HTML and parsed JSON, resumes from the last saved page, and stops (rather than retrying or bypassing) on any challenge, block, or rate-limit page.

exception auto_next_pages.BlockedError[source]

Raised when the site appears to be blocking, throttling, or challenging requests.

auto_next_pages.run_capture_loop(start_url, pages=None, target_rows=100000, output_dir='data', prefix='gradcafe_page_', json_prefix='applicant_data_page', merged_output='applicant_data.json')[source]

Execute main pagination and capture loop across GradCafe survey pages.

Parameters:

  • start_url (str)

  • pages (int | None)

  • target_rows (int)

  • output_dir (str | Path)

  • prefix (str)

  • json_prefix (str)

  • merged_output (str | Path)

Return type:

list[str]

Cleaning — clean

Transform step: normalize whitespace, missing values, and status labels in scraped rows.

clean.clean_data(records)[source]

Clean raw applicant rows for downstream analysis.

The assignment requires preserving the original raw listing text for traceability while also creating a consistent representation for missing or unavailable fields. This function keeps the raw values in the source record, then stores normalized values in the cleaned structure.

Return type:

List[Dict[str, Any]]

Loading — load_data

Load step of the ETL pipeline: normalize scraped records and upsert them into PostgreSQL.

Rows are keyed by p_id and written with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (p_id) DO UPDATE inside one transaction, so reloading the same data never creates duplicates and a failed batch leaves no partial writes.
